title: A Higher-Order Temporal H-Index for Evolving Networks

problem.claim: Existing higher-order H-index concepts are defined for static networks, while evolving networks require measures that account for temporal reachability.

gap.claim: A temporal extension of the n-th order H-index, including corresponding centrality measures and temporal core decompositions, is needed.

contributions.claim: Extends the n-th order H-index to temporal networks and defines corresponding temporal centrality measures and temporal core decompositions.
Derives decompositions of temporal networks into subgraphs with strong temporal coherence.
Analyzes a recursive computation scheme and develops a scalable streaming algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithms are efficient and that their approach has conceptual validity.
The authors report that the n-th order temporal H-index is a strong heuristic for identifying possible super-spreaders in evolving social networks.
The authors report that the approach detects temporally well-connected components.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines the static-network H-index of a node.
Describes the generalized n-th order H-index and its relation to degree centrality, H-index, and k-core.
Extends the higher-order H-index framework to temporal networks and introduces temporal centrality measures and core decompositions.
States that the temporal H-index respects temporal reachability and supports rankings related to spreading importance, while the decompositions capture temporal coherence.

Presents a recursive computation scheme and streaming algorithm, followed by reported experimental evidence concerning efficiency, conceptual validity, super-spreader heuristics, and temporal component detection.

source_observation.claim: Respecting temporal reachability can make node rankings reflect importance in spreading processes.

interpretation.claim: Centrality measures for evolving networks should model the ordering and feasibility of temporal paths rather than relying only on static connectivity.

application.claim: Use temporally constrained centrality or higher-order indices when prioritizing possible spreaders in evolving interaction networks.

exception.claim: The abstract reports heuristic identification of possible super-spreaders, not definitive prediction or independent validation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal definitions of the temporal H-index, centrality measures, or core decompositions.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not state complexity bounds or streaming-resource requirements.
